title: The Painted Alibi
premise: Estate lawyer Jonah Hartwell is hired by a dying woman, Marguerite Voss, to prove that her brother's murder twenty-five years ago never happened — because the will she wants Jonah to execute names the 'murdered' man as a beneficiary. Digging into the closed case, Jonah uncovers a staged death, a forged inquest, and a found family of witnesses who protected someone they loved. The killer was never a stranger but the family itself, covering for a boy who didn't pull the trigger. At the anniversary dinner, where the town raises its glass to the dead man, Jonah forces the truth into the open: the victim faked his death to escape an abusive patriarch, and the real crime — covered up ever since — belongs to the father. The will, it turns out, is Marguerite's final act of restitution.
about_author: Oscar Kavanagh is a former probate clerk who spent a decade reading other people's secrets in filing cabinets before turning them into fiction. He writes from a coastal town much like the one in his novels, where he claims every neighbor is a character and none have sued him yet.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid Twice
chapters.summary: Jonah Hartwell's POV. A frail Marguerite Voss arrives at Jonah's office, pays a year's retainer in cash, and asks him to prove her brother Edmund's murder never happened — then dies within the hour at a nearby café. Jonah, bound by the retainer and unsettled by the timing, opens the file. Emotional beat: cold professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: A Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In Marguerite's safety deposit box Jonah finds a handwritten will leaving Voss House to 'Edmund Voss, living,' dated three years after his death. The bank manager swears Marguerite visited monthly for decades. Emotional beat: the thrill of an impossible puzzle — and the first hint someone else has been looking for this document.

chapters.title: Twenty-Five Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah travels to the seaside town of Greywater Bay, where Edmund Voss drowned beneath the cliffs in 1999 and his business partner was convicted before dying in prison. Everyone Jonah interviews repeats the same polished story, word for word. Emotional beat: the claustrophobia of a town rehearsing a lie.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah learns the Voss family hosts an annual dinner each October marking Edmund's death — this year's falls in six weeks, and invitations name Jonah as Marguerite's executor. The family patriarch's widow, Celeste, warns Jonah off with terrifying courtesy. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking; hospitality as threat.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Grief
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, with a flashback interleave. A forensic document examiner confirms the will's ink predates its supposed date — Marguerite wrote it while Edmund lived. Jonah realizes she always knew he was alive. Emotional beat: grief reinterpreted as complicity; Jonah's certainty cracks.

chapters.title: The Boy on the Cliff Path
chapters.summary: POV shift to Danny Okafor, now a local boat mechanic, who as a teenager saw someone climb up from the rocks the night Edmund drowned. He's kept quiet for twenty-five years because the person he saw was his own foster mother. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance; the found family begins to surface.

chapters.title: House of Portraits
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Breaking into shuttered Voss House, Jonah finds every portrait of Edmund defaced or turned to the wall — except one hidden in the attic, showing him alive and smiling beside a woman who isn't his wife. Emotional beat: dread mixed with tenderness; the house remembers what people won't say.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. Danny reveals the body pulled from the water wore Edmund's ring but had the wrong teeth — he helped bury the discrepancy because the Voss household sheltered him when no one else would. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth; Danny begs Jonah to stop before the dinner.

chapters.title: The Partner Who Went to Prison
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Visiting the convicted partner's daughter, Jonah learns her father confessed falsely to protect someone — and left a letter he made her swear to open only if 'the glass is raised again.' She refuses to hand it over. Emotional beat: the cost of silence passed down a generation.

chapters.title: Celeste's Version
chapters.summary: Celeste's POV chapter. Celeste recounts the marriage: Edmund's father Aldous ruled the family through money and humiliation, and Edmund begged to disappear. Celeste neither confirms nor denies the staging, but slips Jonah Aldous's old ledger. Emotional beat: a villain revealed to be a survivor of a different crime.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The ledger shows years of payments to a private investigator in Portugal — Aldous hunted his son for a decade after the 'death.' Someone in the family paid the investigator to feed false trails. Emotional beat: the murder wasn't a killing; it was an escape, and the war continued underground.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading My Mail
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah's office is searched, the retainer cash stolen, and a threatening note left quoting the inquest verbatim. A police contact admits the original investigation was steered from above — by the judge who was Aldous's oldest friend. Emotional beat: isolation; the case everyone swore was closed intends to stay closed.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Attic Portrait
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. Danny identifies the portrait woman as Rosa, the Voss housekeeper, who raised half the town's strays including him. Rosa, now in a care home, tells Danny that Edmund didn't drown alone that night — someone went down the cliff path after him. Emotional beat: warmth of found family shadowed by a new suspect.

chapters.title: Rosa's Testimony
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Rosa, lucid one afternoon, describes following Edmund to the cliffs: he met a boat, he chose to go, and the only person who tried to stop him was Aldous — who arrived too late and swore them all to silence to protect Edmund from prosecution for faking evidence against the company. Emotional beat: the whole architecture of the lie revealed as protection.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Letters
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Among Marguerite's effects Jonah finds thirty years of unmailed letters addressed to a Portuguese post office box — and proof she received replies until eighteen months ago, when they stopped. Emotional beat: hope that Edmund may still be alive, and fear of why the letters stopped.

chapters.title: The Empty Glass
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. Days before the anniversary dinner, Danny is attacked and warned to leave town; his boat is burned. He realizes whoever silenced the letters knows the truth is surfacing — and it isn't Aldous, who died years ago. Emotional beat: the protector has become the predator; stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: Executor's Privilege
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the will reading, Jonah formally announces the terms naming a living Edmund, forcing the family to react publicly. Cousin Julian Voss — Aldous's grandson and keeper of the estate — goes pale and demands the will be declared invalid. Emotional beat: Jonah weaponizes procedure; the mask slips in front of witnesses.

chapters.title: Julian's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confesses to the reader alone: he intercepted Marguerite's letters eighteen months ago to protect the estate's sale to developers, which requires Edmund legally dead. He never meant harm — until Danny's burning boat. Emotional beat: banality of greed dressed as duty; the antagonist fully humanized.

chapters.title: The Letter Under Glass
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The partner's daughter, moved by Danny's fire, finally surrenders her father's letter: a full confession of the staged drowning, naming every member of the found family who helped. Jonah now holds legal proof the conviction was false. Emotional beat: the weight of evidence finally matching the weight of love behind it.

chapters.title: Anniversary
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the anniversary dinner, as glasses rise to Edmund, Jonah stands and reads the letter aloud, then presents the will. Julian lunges for the documents; Danny and Rosa's old network of townspeople physically shield Jonah. Police, tipped quietly for weeks, arrest Julian for arson and obstruction. Emotional beat: climax — truth spoken over the ritual built to bury it.

chapters.title: Postmarked Lisbon
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Weeks later, a reply finally comes from the Portuguese post office: Edmund is alive, elderly, and asks only that Marguerite's grave be told he was sorry. He waives his inheritance to the found family — Danny, Rosa's residents, the partner's daughter. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; some reunions happen on paper only.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah executes the amended will, watches Voss House become a home for the people who once lied to keep each other safe, and files the one case everyone swore was closed — properly closed at last. On the office door, a new sign: cases taken only when someone needs an alibi undone. Emotional beat: peace earned; memory and inheritance reconciled into found family.
